reasoning: The requirement demands 15 vertices, but only 8 vertices can be covered by two disjoint cliques of size 4 each. Since every vertex must belong to one of the cliques, it is impossible to assign the remaining 7 vertices. Therefore, no such graph exists.
cot_trace:
We are asked to generate a graph with 15 vertices that consists of exactly 2 vertex-disjoint cliques, each of size 4. Every vertex must belong to one of these cliques, and the only edges in the graph are those within these cliques. So we have 2 cliques of 4 vertices each, total 8 vertices. But we need 15 vertices. That means 7 vertices are not in any clique? But the problem says "Every vertex must belong to one of these cliques". So all 15 vertices must be assigned to the two cliques. But each clique has size 4, so total vertices accommodated is 8. That leaves 7 vertices unassigned. So it's impossible. Therefore UNSATISFIABLE.

But wait: "consists of exactly 2 vertex-disjoint clique(s), each of size 4." That means there are exactly 2 cliques, each of size 4. "Every vertex must belong to one of these cliques" implies that all vertices are in one of the two cliques. But then total vertices would be 8, not 15. So no graph with 15 vertices can satisfy that. Hence UNSATISFIABLE.
